summary: Scare Ridge lookout in Douglas County, Oregon: 30-foot pole tower with L-4 cab built 1948, staffed into the 1970s, removed (1973 per history page); no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 30-foot pole tower topped by an L-4 cab; 14 x 14 foot cabin
facts.status_note: Removed; the history page gives 1973, the register gives no year

events.note: Built 1948 per the register and firelookout.com; 1948 annual report quoted on the history page
August 1951 fire near the Umpqua River (also called the Vincent Creek fire) threatened the station; crews backfired to save it
A teenager was evacuated from the lookout as a precaution while it sat near the northwest edge of a fire (August 1966, Eugene Register-Guard item quoted on history page)
History page says the lookout was removed in 1973; the register says only that it has since been removed
Registered with the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on March 28, 2011; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says staffed into the 1970s and since removed, with no year. The history page gives 1973. The record uses 1973 with the history page as its source; the two do not contradict each other.
The history page spells it Scare Creek Ridge in its 1948 and 1966 items and Scare Ridge elsewhere. The register and firelookout.com use Scare Ridge, which the record keeps.

notes_for_editor: The brief's coordinates (43.77226, -123.70692) match the register. A separate dataset in our records gives 43.76151, -123.70816, about 1.2 km south; that source is not among the three read, so the register's point is kept. Staffing into the 1970s is from the register and firelookout.com; the last staffed year is not given. The 1951 fire has two names in the history page's newspaper quotes; the story reports both rather than choosing. The 1966 item names a 17-year-old, which is left out. The brief's 9.1 m height matches the register's 30 ft. Access is omitted: no source says whether the site can be visited. No source describes the site today. Not searched further: the Douglas County and Western Lane FPA history pages.
